subject: general
question: A sum of money becomes five times its original value in 15 years when invested at a certain simple interest rate. If the sum was invested twice the time at the same rate of interest, what would be the final amount?

options.text: The money becomes 9 times its original value
The money becomes 7 times its original value
The money becomes 6 times its original value
The money becomes 8 times its original value

solution:
**Given:**

A sum of money becomes five times its original value in 15 years at a certain simple interest rate.

**Formula used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = P × R × T / 100

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI)

**Calculation:**

Let the Principal be P.

Amount after 15 years = 5P

⇒ 5P = P + (P × R × 15 / 100)
